text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- U.S. ship with arms for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation anchored somewhere between the island of Hvar and the port of Ploce, waiting for the Bosnian government to sack federal deputy defence minister Hasan Cengic.
- Editorial: The ruling party's popularity would grow if it named the individuals responsible for fraud and corruption.
- There were more than 15,000 insolvent companies by the end of August. Total debts of the economy were 7.7 billion kuna.
- Some 3,000 Croatian refugees are expected to pay a visit to cemeteries in the last Serb-held enclave, now under U.N. control.
- Croatia waits for 170 million dollars in gold and currency reserves of the former Yugoslavia kept in Switzerland's Bank for International Settlements.

- Privredna Banka Zagreb and private entrepreneur Ivica Todoric bought most firms in the privatisation process. Privredna paid 95 million marks to become majority owner of Nama department store, while Todoric paid 64.1 million marks for seven firms. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
